newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's border with Jordan usually quiet.
newsitem.headline: Israel's border with Jordan usually quiet.

text.p: A Jordanian soldier's killing of seven Israeli schoolgirls on Thursday took place at a "peace border" that is usually quiet.
An electronic security fence runs along parts of the frontier between Israel and Jordan, which signed a peace treaty in 1994, but violent incidents are rare.

The spot where the shooting took place is 10 km (six miles) south of the Sea of Galilee. It is a tract of farmland, an island nicknamed "the Island of Peace" where the Jordan and Yarmuk rivers meet. Israel leased the area under the peace accord and entry is through a Jordanian checkpoint.
In geography lessons in school, Israeli children are taught to refer to the frontier with Jordan as the peace border.

The last bloodshed in the area was in June when three Israeli soldiers were killed in a Palestinian guerrilla ambush. It was the first such incident since 1988, when a Jordanian stabbed an Israeli dead after infiltrating.
Here is a description of the border since the establishment of Israel in 1948:

1949 - Ceasefire lines drawn after the first Middle East war set the frontier between Israel and Jordan from the Gulf of Aqaba to the Dead Sea in the south and from the Hula Valley to the Sea of Galilee in the north.

1967 - Israel captures the West Bank from Jordan in another war. The Jordan River becomes a de facto border running from the Sea of Galilee to the Dead Sea. The two countries tacitly cooperate on security issues.

1994 - Israel and Jordan sign peace accord. Israel gives back about 380 square km (147 square miles) to Jordan in border adjustments. The final status of the West Bank is left to talks between Israel and the Palestinians.
